does: it adds the hook h9: POST /hooks/h9 takes deliveries from the source chime (https://chime.example.invalid).

what it sends in: deliveries are verified by the header Chime-Secret holding the hook's secret itself (scheme secret); it sends no delivery id; it sends no timestamp; bodies are unique; the command [/bin/false] turns a verified body into the envelope, handed no credential; its events carry no field of their own; the yard registers its webhook with setwebhook (POST /setWebhook), filling url with the public URL and secret_token with the hook's secret.
the yard makes the signing secret for h9 and keeps it in /synthetic/yard/hooks/h9.secret (mode 0600); the hook names that file, and the value is in no note, event, answer or card. No secret is typed.
the approval gives project in the clear, which the yard sends to the register call with the URL and the secret.
it will call POST /setWebhook at https://chime.example.invalid to register https://hooks.example.invalid/h9.

weight.line: widens who the yard listens to: POST /hooks/h9 takes deliveries from outside the yard for the source chime
